sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b} = 10] and [MATH: \dfrac{50a}{m b} = 5,] what is the value of [MATH: m?]
sections.readable_text: If [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b} = 10] and [MATH: \dfrac{50a}{m b} = 5,] what is the value of [MATH: m?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the relations

  • [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b} = 10,]

  • [MATH: \dfrac{50a}{m b} = 5.]

Let's substitute [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b}=10] into the second equation and simplify: [MATH: (50a)/(mb)|= 5; (50)/(m) ⋅ (a)/(b)|= 5; (50)/(m) ⋅ 10|= 5; (500)/(m)|= 5; 500|= 5m; m|= (500)/(5); m|= 100]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: m] is [MATH: 100.]

sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: \dfrac{2.7\,m}{n} = 5.4] and [MATH: \dfrac{m}{nt} = 16,] what is the value of [MATH: t?]
sections.readable_text: If [MATH: \dfrac{2.7\,m}{n} = 5.4] and [MATH: \dfrac{m}{nt} = 16,] what is the value of [MATH: t?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given two equations [MATH: \dfrac{2.7\,m}{n}=5.4 \quad \text{and} \quad \dfrac{m}{nt}=16.]

First, we solve the first equation for [MATH: \dfrac{m}{n}{:}] [MATH: \dfrac{m}{n}=\dfrac{5.4}{2.7}=2.]

Now, we substitute [MATH: \dfrac{m}{n}=2] into the second equation and solve for [MATH: t{:}] [MATH: (m)/(nt)|= 16; (m)/(n) ⋅ (1)/(t)|= 16; 2 ⋅ (1)/(t)|= 16; (2)/(t)|= 16; 2|= 16t; t|= (2)/(16); t|= 0.125]

So, the value of [MATH: t] is [MATH: 0.125.]

Item 2 — Example: Using Equal Proportions to Compute a Coefficient

Example Prompt:
If [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b} = 10] and [MATH: \dfrac{50a}{m b} = 5,] what is the value of [MATH: m?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We are given the relations

- [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b} = 10,]
- [MATH: \dfrac{50a}{m b} = 5.]

Let's substitute [MATH: \dfrac{a}{b}=10] into the second equation and simplify:
[MATH: (50a)/(mb)|= 5; (50)/(m) ⋅ (a)/(b)|= 5; (50)/(m) ⋅ 10|= 5; (500)/(m)|= 5; 500|= 5m; m|= (500)/(5); m|= 100]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: m] is [MATH: 100.]

[MATH: \dfrac{m}{n}=\dfrac{5.4}{2.7}=2.]

Now, we substitute [MATH: \dfrac{m}{n}=2] into the second equation and solve for [MATH: t{:}]
[MATH: (m)/(nt)|= 16; (m)/(n) ⋅ (1)/(t)|= 16; 2 ⋅ (1)/(t)|= 16; (2)/(t)|= 16; 2|= 16t; t|= (2)/(16); t|= 0.125]

So, the value of [MATH: t] is [MATH: 0.125.]
